meta.label: Sleep debt
meta.rationale: Computed from several measurements; inherits their confidence.

text: Accumulated shortfall against your sleep need, with old debt fading: each night, debt = 0.794 × yesterday's debt + (need − sleep). The decay alone halves standing debt in 3 nights.

That is tuned to how recovery actually feels — one bad night absorbed, two or three compounding, a few solid nights restoring — rather than to the recovery literature, which finds objective recovery slower than the subjective kind. So treat a cleared number as encouraging rather than as proof, and read the 30-day line on the chart for the long-run picture.

The subtraction is symmetric and has no floor: sleeping past your need repays debt hour for hour, and a sustained surplus can carry debt below zero, because banked sleep genuinely buys resilience. Naps count as sleep. A night with no recording holds debt where it is — an unworn ring is not evidence you caught up.

One thing to understand before reading the level: the need you grade against sets the zero point and almost nothing else. Moving need by an hour moves every debt reading by about 5 hours, while the shape of the line stays the same — debt computed against your median sleep correlates 0.99 with this. So read the movement, not the level, and act on sleep opportunity, which you control.

components.label: Structural floor
components.note: where debt sits if you keep sleeping your median
